reason: The text fragment from Job 1-2 portrays Yahweh as benevolent toward Job, an exemplary Hebrew person. Yahweh abundantly blesses Job with wealth, children, and respect, and describes him approvingly as 'perfect and upright, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil.' When Job suffers, it is Satan—not Yahweh—who causes the destruction, and Yahweh explicitly permits this only as a test while protecting Job's life. Job responds with faith and blessing: 'The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.' The text emphasizes Job's righteousness even amid suffering ('Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly'). Throughout, Yahweh is shown protecting and favoring the faithful Hebrew, not antagonism.
